svg.text: One accessor, and NULL means "inherit from the deployment"
the stored row
every column nullable. Only
what was written is set.
the deployment
the environment file, as
every install has always had
one accessor
overlays, re-validates every
endpoint, caches 60 seconds
the effective value
plus where it came from
The console always displays two things per setting: the value in force, and whether it is inherited or set here.
Rejected: a migration that seeds the row from the environment
It would make the migration's result depend on which container happened to run it.
Worse, it would freeze the deployment's value at upgrade time, so an operator who later
edited the environment file would find it silently ignored.
Which is the reverse of the property this change exists to give them. A row that comes into being only when
an administrator first writes a setting is what buys a no-op upgrade for free.
Two escape hatches, deliberately different in kind
A flag that ignores the row entirely
Recovers a stored value that has broken the product. While it is set, the console shows a banner saying so,
otherwise it becomes a way to make an administrator believe they changed something.
A time-boxed grant, not a second flag
A flag left on after an incident is indistinguishable from one that was never set. Expiry is the difference.
